name: knowledgec_query
description: Read knowledgeC.db, the application and device-state records macOS keeps for its own features (not an audit log): for each ZOBJECT row its stream, typed values (value_string, value_integer, value_double, value_type_code: the lock and backlight states are integers), raw and converted start, end and creation times (Apple epoch, 2001-01-01 UTC, to ISO 8601 UTC with the raw value kept), UUID, the other non-null ZOBJECT columns and, joined on the row's own foreign keys, every non-null column of its ZSTRUCTUREDMETADATA and ZSOURCE rows under their own names. The joins are made from the schema the file has; the answer says which tables joined, lists the tables and columns and carries a fingerprint of the three tables' columns. A stream's meaning, and whether it exists, depends on the build and the device: every stream in the file is inventoried (count, first and last start) whatever the filters, and none is assumed. since and until filter by start time (a record that began earlier and overlapped the window is not selected); a filter the database has no column for is listed in filters_unapplied and the answer is partial. A write-ahead log beside the database holds committed rows the main file lacks; a rollback journal holds the old pages of a transaction that did not commit and holds no such rows (a journal that is not a valid hot journal, 3,000 random bytes say, is removed by SQLite without changing the database, and the answer says that and does not call it a rollback). With either, the files are copied to a private directory, SQLite works on the copy (WAL frames applied are counted; a hot journal is rolled back in the copy, reported in source_used.journal and in problems because the copy's state is then not the main file's), and the copy is removed, so the evidence directory is never written to; without a sidecar the file is opened read-only and immutable. What it does not measure: Biome streams, other databases, whether a screen or focus state shows a person at the keyboard (it does not), or whether the stream was complete (retention varies). Every row carries its Z_PK and parser; rows are ordered by start then Z_PK; they are written to out_file as they are read (an existing file or link there is refused), or paged losslessly to a file the answer names. Cells are read bounded, and a statement never loads a TEXT cell: a TEXT cell is read through a blob handle (on a second connection that is replaced every 20,000 handles, since CPython's sqlite3 keeps a weak reference to each handle until its connection closes), a BLOB longer than 4096 bytes is not read at all but for its head, and a TEXT or BLOB value longer than 4096 characters or bytes is returned as its first 4096, its whole byte length, _truncated and where the whole is in the database (_where: table, column, rowid): a 300 MB TEXT cell costs about 30 MB of memory, not 324. A BLOB's head is hexadecimal (_hex), not base64. On a Python without blob handles (before 3.11) a statement reads a TEXT cell whole. export_oversize: true, in a job run as secret output, streams each whole value to a private file (mode 0600) under $OUT/tool-output/knowledgec-values/ and names it (max_export_bytes bounds the total). The inline answer is cut at max_inline_bytes as well as at limit, and a rerun that finds fewer rows does not replace a larger earlier page file (it writes a new name and says which it kept). A schema it cannot read (a virtual table whose module is missing), a ZOBJECT with no ZSTREAMNAME and an unapplied filter are named in problems and the answer is partial. The tool has a clock of its own, max_seconds (default 80, at most 90, below the 120 seconds of the manifest; staging, the stream inventory, the clean-up and the answer come after it): a progress handler aborts the statement when it passes, so even the sort of a table with millions of rows is stopped, and the rows are checked against it every 256. When it passes, or a stop signal arrives, status is partial, the entries are a prefix of the result in start order (the whole prefix is in the file the answer names, and out_file is kept), and resume gives rows_read, stopped_after_z_pk, last_start_raw and resume_since (a microsecond before the last start read), the since to run again with; the rows at the last start are read twice. SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it the same way: one JSON answer with interrupted set to the signal's name, exit 128 plus the signal, the staged copy of the database removed. A database whose schema holds text that is not UTF-8 (SQLite's own error message then cannot be decoded) is a JSON refusal, not a traceback. Every answer and refusal carries status (complete, partial or failed) and status_basis. out_file is created with mode 0600. SENSITIVE: the values, URLs (a Safari history or web-usage value can carry a token in its query string), bundle and device ids, other columns and a BLOB's head are evidence text. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). The windows-forensics pack's shared boundary block, copied byte for byte (a test holds the copies equal), judges every key and value of the answer, of an error answer, and of every row of every file this tool writes, by the type of the field it fills: a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain); free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld; and a second check, written apart from the first, reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Past the judging time (10 seconds for an answer or a row, and never past the seal stop of the tool) the strings the evidence supplied are no longer judged: each is replaced whole and the answer is partial, except the names this tool wrote itself and a string of 15 characters or fewer made only of letters, digits, _ and . that does not start like a vendor token. write_values: true writes the originals of everything the boundary withheld to knowledgec_query-values.jsonl under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced); it and export_oversize are accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares both; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants in a value, in another ZOBJECT column, in a BLOB's head and as the name of a column (rates, not guarantees, from one seeded run of 1,000 plants per shape; tests/pack-macos-forensics-boundary.test.ts plants 300 per shape and asserts the bounds). Of the 21 shapes the boundary claims (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google and npm tokens, AWS key ids, JWT, PEM private keys, user-info with an @ in the password, Password= and password: values, NUL and zero-width splits, base64 keys of 16, 20 and 32 bytes, AWS-shaped keys of 40 characters, random base62 of 24 and 40 characters) 20 were printed whole in 0 of 1,000 plants and random base62 of 24 characters in 1 of 1,000 (0.1%); a piece of 12 characters of an AWS-shaped key and of a random base62 token was printed in 1 of 1,000 plants each. The shapes it does not claim are printed: a plain password, a four-word passphrase and a UUID-shaped key, 1,000 of 1,000. The 47 column names of a knowledgeC schema written from Apple's CoreData naming pass unchanged; no real knowledgeC database was at hand to measure what it costs on one. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name, random bytes with no text in them, anything under 16 characters in a name): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more, unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more, and the query values of a URL. Column names are shown (the names of a real knowledgeC schema pass).

db.description: A knowledgeC.db; any -wal, -shm or -journal beside it is used (in a private copy), so copy them out together

stream.description: A stream name or a LIKE pattern, e.g. '/app/inFocus' or '/app/%'

since.description: Only entries starting at or after this ISO 8601 UTC time (needs a ZSTARTDATE column; otherwise listed in filters_unapplied)

until.description: Only entries starting at or before this ISO 8601 UTC time (same)

limit.description: Entries shown inline (default 500). All are counted; the whole result is in out_file, or, when that is omitted, in a file under work/<your id>/tool-output/ (in a job, $OUT/tool-output/) that the answer names

out_file.description: JSONL path for every matching entry (each row judged by the boundary), written as each is read, mode 0600. The tool does not overwrite: an existing file or link at that name is refused

max_stage_bytes.description: The database and its sidecars are copied only up to this many bytes in all (default 2147483648); over it nothing is read and the answer says so

max_inline_bytes.description: The inline entries are cut at this many bytes as well as at `limit` entries (default 1048576); the whole is in out_file or the file the answer names

export_oversize.description: Write each TEXT or BLOB value longer than 4096 characters or bytes, whole, to a private file under $OUT/tool-output/knowledgec-values/ and name it in the cell. Only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false

max_export_bytes.description: export_oversize writes at most this many bytes in all (default 1073741824); a value that would pass it is not written and the answer says so

max_seconds.description: The tool's own clock (default 80, at most 90): when it passes the read stops, status is partial and resume says how to go on; a larger value is clamped and the answer says so

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to $OUT/knowledgec_query-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
